posts.content_md:
Do we have any OSA members?

I am interested in joining but I am not sure if it would benefit me. I find papers they publish that I would like to read all of the time but they have so many Journals I don't even know which ones are which.

Any thoughts?

posts.author: favalora
posts.content_md:
Colin -

I'm a member of the OSA and the SPIE.

I subscribe to the OSA's *Optics Letters*and *Applied Optics*. These cover the range of what I'm interested in. *Optics Letters* is supposed to cover "science" (fundamental stuff) and *Applied Optics* is supposed to cover "applied science" (engineering). In reality, you can find applied science in both, which is fortunate for me. You should go online and look at the last few months' table of contents. As I said, you'll see that *Applied Optics* covers a very broad array of optical instruments, diffractive systems, etc., but similar topics - if of hopefully "extraordinary" merit - find their way into Optics Letters.

I very much enjoy the ability to have full-text access to historic articles of Optics Letters online.

Remember the SPIE, too. I susbscribe to *Optical Engineering*, edited by O'Shea. [Link to OE](http://www.spie.org/app/Publications/index.cfm?fuseaction=journals&type=oe)

In addition, with respect to holography, see their annual conference called "Practical Holography." It is full of hands-on applicable research:

[link to 2006 conference program](http://spie.org/Conferences/Programs/06/pw/opto/index.cfm?fuseaction=6136)

I recommend you purchase the annual proceedings.

Also, the SPIE has a holography society, which publishes a newsletter.

gregg
